title: Models, tiers and cost
scope: Choosing a model for the work, what each tier is good for, and the token cost of adversarial passes. Excludes which roles exist (see crews-and-roles).

statements.statement: I’m pretty sure the implementers are on sonnet -> opus modeling because they get 8 tries each to go green. Fable is only useful if the workflow is trying to one shot the solution.
statements.context: Watching the first build run and asking whether it was using tiered agents.

statements.statement: if it’s retry until green fable will blow the budget as an implementer.
send explorers when ever you want, they are cheap and don't spoil context.
statements.context: Telling the interviewer to stop asking permission to research.

statements.statement: these bulk adversaries are costing huge tokens and later runs are less valuable than earlier runs.
statements.context: Refusing a second attacker pass over the spec.

statements.statement: one Sonnet recommendation was not a rule that all crew be Sonnet. Choose the model for the work.
statements.context: Correcting a cockpit rule the pilot had written from a single research finding.

statements.statement: Sonnet doesn't have the CPU power to process this type of work and takes extensively longer and sometimes busts. Research has found opus to keep up as an adversary.
statements.context: Ruling on the research team's makeup.
